raw_case_text:
In Oct 2017, a 32-year-old male presented with intermittent bleeding per-rectum after defecation for 40 days with associated cough and fever. The patient had noticed a mass over the anus for five years but did not seek treatment as the lesion was not painful. He had visited the surgical unit at Gondar University Hospital, and he was under investigation for possible colorectal carcinoma.
At the presentation, he was well-looking, with normal vital signs. On abdominal examination, he had a spleen palpable 5 cm below the left costal margin, a liver palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin, and a 5 cm by 5 cm erythematous nontender plaque over the inner right buttock, perianal area. Per-rectum examination showed a circumferential firm rectal swelling 4 cm from the anal verge.
The abdominal CT scan showed a circumferential rectal mass 2.5 cm thick with extension to the mesorectum and thickening of the mesorectal facia (suggestive of rectal cancer with rectal and mesorectal extension). It also showed mesorectal lymphadenopathy (stage III) and hepatosplenomegaly. The conclusion of the CT scan was rectal cancer plus hepatosplenomegaly. Chest X-ray was normal.
An endoscopic biopsy from the rectum showed three fragments with unremarkable mucosa except for focal ulceration. The submucosa showed intense lymphocytic inflammation, and numerous macrophages were stuffed with intracellular Leishmania amastigotes. No feature of malignancy was seen in the biopsy. Fine needle aspiration (FNA) from the perianal lesion showed Leishman Donovan bodies (grade+3 amastigotes). Splenic aspiration was carried out to rule out concomitant VL but was negative for Leishmania amastigotes. An HIV test was carried out at admission, and he was found to be seropositive with a CD4 count of 306.
The patient was treated with (liposomal amphotericin B) AmBisome 5 mg/kg for 8 doses initially after which rectal bleeding stopped, and his fever recovered. On physical examination, he had a perianal 4 cm by 2 cm mass with central ulceration, which had decreased in size but still showed an active CL lesion. Therefore, treatment was extended with AmBisome 5 mg/kg for 8 doses plus miltefosine 100 mg for 28 days (2 x 50 mg daily). Antiretroviral therapy was planned to be initiated after counseling.
After treatment completion, the perianal mass flattened to 3 by 2 cm, with no significant rectal mass appreciated on physical examination. Fine needle aspiration from the perianal healed lesion was negative for Leishman Donovan bodies. A repeated abdominal CT scan showed a circumferential rectal mass of 1 cm and splenomegaly, indicating a reduction in the rectal lesion size. The patient was followed for 2 years, without any recurrence.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 32-year-old male presented with intermittent bleeding per-rectum after defecation for 40 days, accompanied by cough and fever.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient noticed a painless perianal mass 5 years prior to presentation, for which he did not seek treatment. Forty days prior to presentation, he developed intermittent post-defecation rectal bleeding associated with fever and cough, and was subsequently investigated for suspected colorectal carcinoma.
subjective.past_medical_history: Five-year history of an untreated painless perianal mass. No other prior medical conditions, hospitalizations, or travel documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports fever and cough; denies pain associated with the perianal lesion.

objective.physical_examination: Well-appearing with normal vital signs. Abdomen: spleen palpable 5 cm below the left costal margin, liver palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin; a 5 cm x 5 cm erythematous nontender plaque over the inner right buttock and perianal area. Digital rectal examination: circumferential firm rectal swelling 4 cm from the anal verge.
objective.routine_investigations: Chest X-ray: normal. CD4 count: 306 cells/muL.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal CT scan: circumferential rectal mass 2.5 cm thick with extension to the mesorectum, thickening of the mesorectal fascia (suggestive of rectal cancer with rectal and mesorectal extension), mesorectal lymphadenopathy (stage III), and hepatosplenomegaly. Endoscopic rectal biopsy: unremarkable mucosa except for focal ulceration, submucosa with intense lymphocytic inflammation and numerous macrophages with intracellular structures; no features of malignancy. Fine needle aspiration (FNA) of perianal lesion: cellular aspirate with macrophage infiltration. Splenic aspiration: negative for parasites.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Endoscopic rectal biopsy demonstrated numerous macrophages stuffed with intracellular Leishmania amastigotes. Fine needle aspiration (FNA) from the perianal lesion confirmed Leishman-Donovan bodies (grade +3 amastigotes). Splenic aspiration was negative for Leishmania amastigotes, excluding concomitant visceral leishmaniasis. HIV serology was positive (CD4 306 cells/muL). Malignancy ruled out on endoscopic biopsy. Treatment and Outcome: Initiated on liposomal amphotericin B (AmBisome) 5 mg/kg for 8 doses, resulting in cessation of rectal bleeding and resolution of fever. The perianal lesion decreased to 4 cm x 2 cm with central ulceration. Treatment was extended with AmBisome 5 mg/kg for 8 additional doses plus oral miltefosine 100 mg daily (50 mg twice daily) for 28 days, alongside planned antiretroviral therapy counseling. Following therapy, the perianal mass flattened to 3 cm x 2 cm, repeat FNA was negative for Leishman-Donovan bodies, and repeat abdominal CT showed reduction of the circumferential rectal mass to 1 cm with residual splenomegaly. No recurrence at 2-year follow-up.
